extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for NeurIPS 2024 (program committee: reviewers assigned to papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for reviewers assigned to NeurIPS 2024 submissions, including procedural responsibilities, the review form dimensions (summary, strengths/weaknesses, ratings), and best practices for discussion, ethics, and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: agree to Code of Conduct and update OpenReview profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct. Make sure your OpenReview profile is up to date and the preferred email address is correct so conference communications reach you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm preferred email in OpenReview; whitelist noreply@openreview.net if messages are marked as spam. Assignments and tasks appear at the reviewer console in OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must bid on papers during the bidding window; bids are an important input to the paper matching process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidding dates provided. Deceptive bidding to influence outcomes is prohibited and may trigger an ethics investigation and removal from future involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check paper assignments and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you are notified of papers to review, log in to OpenReview to check for conflicts and verify that papers fall within your area of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don’t feel qualified to review an assigned paper, communicate this to your Area Chair (AC) right away. Assignments may change during the first week.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write thoughtful, informative, and substantiated reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your review as informative and substantiated as possible; superficial, uninformed reviews are worse than no review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the review form questions and guidance. Flag questionable papers for ethics review. Use the NeurIPS paper checklist as a tool. Do not worry about minor formatting violations, but report major violations to your AC. Reviews and meta-reviews of accepted papers (and opted-in rejected papers) will be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in reading author responses and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Read author responses and other reviews carefully during the discussion period and participate constructively in discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an open mind; acknowledge that you have read and considered responses. Revise your review if your evaluation changes and explain why. Participating is critical for borderline papers and those with reviewer disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect deadlines for reviews and discussion participation; if you cannot complete on time, notify the AC as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to AC questions during decision phases. If an emergency prevents meeting a deadline, contact your AC to provide a revised timeline or state you cannot complete the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the NeurIPS paper checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to use the NeurIPS paper checklist included in each paper as a tool when preparing reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some submissions may include the checklist in supplementary material. Answering 'no' to some checklist questions is typically not grounds for rejection; authors should be rewarded for being upfront about limitations and possible negative impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not invite sub-reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-reviewers are not allowed to help with reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts of interest cannot be properly checked for sub-reviewers, and they could not participate properly in the discussion phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything relating to the review process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they become publicly available. Do not talk about or share submissions without prior approval from the program chairs. Submitted code cannot be distributed or used for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs — reviewers and ACs cannot see author identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for anonymizing submissions (including supplementary/linked material). If a submission is not adequately anonymized, contact the AC. Do not attempt to find out author identities (e.g., by searching arXiv); doing so would violate the policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting instructions for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to nine content pages in the NeurIPS submission style; additional pages containing only references and the NeurIPS 2024 paper checklist are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content beyond that (including supplementary material) can be reviewed at reviewer discretion. Minor formatting violations (e.g., spillover to page 10) were handled leniently if easily rectified; flag violations that are not easily rectified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS does not allow submissions identical or substantially similar to papers submitted to or published in other archival venues or other NeurIPS submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slicing contributions too thinly is discouraged and may violate the policy. If you suspect a dual submission, contact the corresponding AC. See Call for Papers and FAQ for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing submitted code and clicking links safely
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities; exercise caution when running submitted code or following links provided in submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run code inside a secure environment (recommended: Docker container, virtual machine, or network-isolated cloud instance). Be cautious about accessing external links which may contain vulnerabilities or log IP addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging ethical concerns / request ethics review
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are ethical issues with a paper, flag the paper for an ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flagged papers will be assigned ethics reviewers who join the paper's program committee; refer to the NeurIPS ethics guidelines for when this is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (review form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary of the paper and its contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not the place to critique the paper; authors should generally agree with a well-written summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and weaknesses (review form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a thorough assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of the paper, touching on key dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address each of the listed dimensions (originality, quality, clarity, significance). Be specific and constructive so authors, other reviewers, and ACs can act on feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (strengths/weaknesses sub-dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the tasks or methods new? Is the work a novel combination of well-known techniques? Is it clear how this work differs from previous contributions? Is related work adequately cited?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel combinations can be valuable. Explicitly state how the work differs from prior work and whether related work is properly acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality (strengths/weaknesses sub-dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the submission technically sound? Are claims well supported by theoretical analysis or experimental results? Are methods appropriate? Is this a complete piece of work or work in progress?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether authors are careful and honest about evaluating strengths and weaknesses; check that claims are adequately supported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (strengths/weaknesses sub-dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the submission clearly written and well organized? Does it adequately inform the reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear, provide constructive suggestions for improving clarity. A superbly written paper provides enough information for an expert reader to reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (strengths/weaknesses sub-dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the results important? Are researchers or practitioners likely to use the ideas or build on them? Does the submission address a difficult task better than previous work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the work advances the state of the art in a demonstrable way, or provides unique data, conclusions, or theoretical/experimental approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and suggestions for authors (review form)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and carefully describe questions and suggestions that, if answered, could change your opinion, clarify confusion, or address limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are important for a productive rebuttal and discussion phase with authors; prioritize points that can be addressed in the author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and potential negative societal impact (review form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the authors have adequately addressed limitations and potential negative societal impacts of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not addressed, include constructive suggestions. Authors should be rewarded rather than punished for being upfront about limitations and negative impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness rating (numeric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a numerical rating (4-1) indicating the soundness of technical claims, experimental and research methodology, and whether central claims are adequately supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 = excellent, 3 = good, 2 = fair, 1 = poor. Use this to reflect rigor and support for claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation rating (numeric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a numerical rating (4-1) for the quality of presentation, including writing style, clarity, and contextualization relative to prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 4 = excellent, 3 = good, 2 = fair, 1 = poor. Consider both writing quality and how well the paper situates itself in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution rating (numeric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a numerical rating (4-1) for the quality of the overall contribution the paper makes to the research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider importance of questions asked, originality of ideas or execution, and value of results to the NeurIPS community. 4 = excellent, 3 = good, 2 = fair, 1 = poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (1-10) with guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall score (1-10) for the submission with detailed qualitative anchors from 'Very Strong Reject' to 'Award quality'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed mappings provided (examples): 10 = award quality, technically flawless with groundbreaking impact; 9 = very strong accept; 8 = strong accept; 7 = accept; 6 = weak accept; 5 = borderline accept; 4 = borderline reject; 3 = reject; 2 = strong reject; 1 = very strong reject. Use these descriptions to calibrate overall assessment considering technical quality, impact, evaluation, reproducibility, and ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a confidence score (1-5) indicating how confident you are in your evaluation of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 = absolutely certain and very familiar with related work; 4 = confident but not absolutely certain; 3 = fairly confident; 2 = willing to defend but likely unfamiliar with central parts; 1 = an educated guess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that you have and will continue to abide by the NeurIPS Code Of Conduct while performing reviewer duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required checkbox/acknowledgement when submitting reviews and participating in discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: General reviewer behavior guidelines: be thoughtful, be fair, be useful, be specific, be flexible, be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be constructive to avoid crushing early-career authors, avoid letting personal feelings affect reviews, provide feedback useful to authors/other reviewers/ACs, avoid vague statements, update understanding and reviews when new information is presented, and respect deadlines. If pressured to provide a particular outcome or you notice unethical behavior, notify program chairs or AC as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling suspected plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: If you suspect plagiarism in a submission, reach out to your AC and explain the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AC guidance; ACs have mechanisms to investigate and escalate as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading prior reviews for resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Never break anonymity; do not base your review solely on previous reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if you’ve seen a previous version, treat the submission as a new submission — read it carefully and write an independent, high-quality review.
